name: Sonnet macro/sector rotation
strategy: Positioning for a 2026 macro backdrop of continued Fed easing, a softer dollar, sticky-but-moderating inflation, and reaccelerating global industrial/capex activity (AI infrastructure buildout, grid/power investment, reshoring). Rotate into rate-sensitive cyclicals (financials, homebuilders/industrials), commodities/gold as a dollar-debasement and geopolitical hedge, international/EM equities benefiting from a weaker USD, and power/infrastructure plays tied to AI-driven electricity demand, while trimming pure mega-cap-tech concentration in favor of broader participation (small/mid caps via financials and industrials).

orders.reason: Gold miner-specific execution/cost risk has offset the Fed-easing/weak-dollar tailwind (-13.7% H1); rotate to cleaner bullion exposure.
Physical gold is a purer play on continued Fed easing, softer dollar, and sticky inflation hedging without miner operating risk.
Uranium thesis stalled (-11.2% H1) amid policy/permitting overhangs; capital better deployed into the broader industrial capex re-acceleration theme.
Semiconductors are the direct beneficiary of reaccelerating global industrial/AI capex spending, complementing existing industrial and EM cyclical exposure.

outlook: H2 2026 should favor continued cyclical/industrial and EM strength as the Fed keeps easing and the dollar stays soft, while gold and semis add convexity to that macro backdrop; energy, industrials, and financials remain core holds into year-end.
